about: Panels of the results explorer (BOM-37). Each reads one public result file from this repository; nothing here or in the files is corpus text. mode: rows (an object whose keys become the first column, or a list of objects), counts (an object of label -> number), csv. Columns may be dotted paths into each row. A panel marked pending shows a placeholder until its file exists.

panels.title: Can each method tell authors apart? (validation benchmark)
panels.explain: Closed set: share of test samples assigned to the right author among the candidates. False matches (open_set_fpr): share of samples a method wrongly accepts as a candidate's when the true author is absent (Amendment 25). A method passes with closed set at least 0.90 and false matches at most 0.05. None passes.

panels.title: Our methods against published ones, on equal terms (BOM-68)
panels.explain: Every method on the same tests. 'trials' are the benchmark's own samples; 'tails' are the held-out tests the fine-tuned language models use. alm_gpt2 rows use a modern GPT-2 as the base model instead of our 1780-1830 models.

panels.title: Head to head on identical tests (BOM-68)
panels.explain: For each pair of methods, how many tests only the first got right, how many only the second, and an exact McNemar p-value.

panels.title: Candidate-author language models on their own held-out text (BOM-28, 297M)
panels.explain: One model per candidate writing sample and per control group. Closed set: share of the unit's held-out windows the right model claims. Units with no tests were too short to hold any text out.

panels.title: Does imitating scripture fool the method? (BOM-31)
panels.explain: Forward: authors' imitation-scripture writing tested against references from their ordinary prose. Weight is section 9's down-weighting: 1 at 80% or better, 0.5 at 60%, else 0.

panels.title: Proposed sources in the paraphrase search (BOM-25)
panels.explain: Each proposed source ranked within its registered control group by paraphrase density (parallels per 10,000 words of Book of Mormon text). Rank 1 means densest in its group; whether that stands out is judged against a null (named_null.json).

panels.title: What explains the look-alike passages? (BOM-26)
panels.explain: 1,069 matched passage pairs sorted by a model into BIBLICAL (King James wording), COMMON (period stock phrasing) or SPECIFIC. A simulated second review (another model, blind) relabelled both SPECIFIC pairs COMMON: none is specific under both.

panels.title: Dating text by its grammar: accuracy on held-out authors (BOM-29)
panels.explain: Mean error of the predicted year, how often the 90% interval holds the true year, and the share of segments whose median falls in 1780-1830.

panels.title: Corrections in the manuscripts (BOM-34)
panels.explain: Original: the dictated manuscript (231 surviving pages). Printers: the copy made for the printer. Sound-alike fixes (where/were) are far commoner in the dictated copy: the trace of writing from dictation. Counts and types only, no manuscript text.

panels.title: Could Joseph Smith have read it before mid-1829? (BOM-33)
panels.explain: 3: documented within his reach (local library, local bookstore ad). 2: documented in western or central New York. 1: in print in the US only. 0: no evidence it circulated in the US before 1829. Evidence is our summary with citations.

panels.title: The author sweep: can it find a known author? (BOM-39, BOM-47)
panels.explain: Calibration on 200 books by authors the style model never saw: how often the true author comes first, and how many wrong authors clear the lead bar by chance.

panels.title: Blind run on the Book of Mormon (BOM-32)
panels.explain: Published after the blind run is unblinded.

panels.title: Everything combined, per model size (BOM-35)
panels.explain: Probability for each candidate and for 'not in the set', one column per model size.
